instrument_name: N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.2 Time and mode of payment; paydays (Wage Payment Law), as reprinted by NJDOL
authority: NJ Legislature (text as published by NJ DOL Wage and Hour Compliance, Selected NJ State Labor Laws)
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay full wages at least twice each calendar month on regular paydays designated in advance; bona fide executive/supervisory/special classes (reg: overtime-exempt under N.J.A.C. 12:56-7) may be paid less often but at least once a month. Payday on a nonwork day -> preceding work day (unless CBA). Pay period must end not more than 10 working days before the payday. Payment in US money or checks cashable without difficulty; employer bears check-cashing fee at the drawee bank and check-deposit-return fees (12:55-2.4(e)-(g)).
verification_method: inspected directly (statute and regulation text read)

instrument_name: N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.2a and N.J.A.C. 12:55-2.4(h),(i) Direct deposit and payroll debit card
authority: NJ Legislature / NJ DOL (text as published by NJ DOL)
figure_or_rule_carried: Direct deposit only with the employee's prior written consent, obtained without coercion, not a condition of hire or continued employment; employee may revoke on timely notice. Payroll debit card: prior written consent (same conditions); prior written disclosure of all card features and fees; at least one free full withdrawal per pay period in US money; employee may opt out to check or direct deposit. Statement of deductions still furnished each pay period.
verification_method: inspected directly (statute and regulation text read)

instrument_name: N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.3 Termination or suspension of employment; N.J.A.C. 12:55-2.4(a)-(c)
authority: NJ Legislature / NJ DOL (text as published by NJ DOL)
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge, layoff, suspension or quit for any reason: all wages due not later than the regular payday for the pay period in which employment ended (incentive pay: reasonable approximation until computed); labor-dispute suspension involving payroll staff: +10 days. Paid through regular channels or by mail if the employee requests. Regulation 12:55-2.4(a) words it as final payment within 10 days from the end of the work period, in compliance with 34:11-4.2. Same rule for discharge and resignation. Accrued vacation: no statutory payout; the Wage Payment Law enforces only the benefits the employer agreed to provide (NJ DOL Wage Payment page, 'Fringe Benefits').
verification_method: inspected directly (statute and regulation text read)

instrument_name: N.J.S.A. 34:11-4.4 Withholding from wages; 34:11-4.4a; N.J.A.C. 12:55-2.1 to 2.3
authority: NJ Legislature / NJ DOL (text as published by NJ DOL)

instrument_name: NJDOL Earned Sick Leave: What Employers Need to Know (MW-566, 12/23) - N.J.S.A. 34:11D-1 et seq.
authority: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers, all sizes; full/part-time, temporary, seasonal. Exempt: union construction workers, per diem health care, public employees with full-pay sick leave under other law. Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked up to 40 hours per benefit year, or front-load at least 40 hours (may prorate new hires). Usable from day 120 of employment. Employer-fixed 12-month benefit year (30 days notice to NJDOL to change). Paid at the normal rate and at least the State minimum wage, in the same or next pay period. Unused: carry over (use capped at 40 h/yr) or pay out at end of benefit year. Documentation after 3+ consecutive days. Records 5 years. Notice in the employee's primary language if NJDOL publishes it.

instrument_name: NJDOL Wage and Hour Compliance FAQs (for Workers) - minimum wage, overtime, deductions, pay frequency, minors
authority: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Wage and Hour Compliance
article_or_section: Minimum Wage; Overtime; Payroll Deductions; Frequency of Payment; Benefits; Minors
figure_or_rule_carried: Banner: from 2027-01-01 minimum wage 16.48 USD/h for most workers. Overtime 1.5x regular rate for hours actually worked over 40 in a 7-day workweek (no daily overtime; no holiday/weekend premium; paid holiday hours do not count; not waivable); multiple rates -> weighted average, half-time premium. Exempt from minimum wage: automobile salespersons, outside salespersons, minors under 18 except in listed industries (retail, food service, first processing of farm products, beauty culture, laundry/cleaning/dyeing, light manufacturing/apparel, hotel/motel). Exempt-salaried: executive, administrative, professional. No deductions for shortages, breakage, damage, unreturned property, pre-employment testing, uniforms, or job-required licenses. Pay-statement content per FAQ: gross, net and itemized deductions, electronic or paper. Fringe benefits (vacation, severance, holiday) not required by NJ law; if provided, administered per policy. Minors under 18: 30-minute meal period after 5 consecutive hours; working papers for all under 18. 6-year statute of limitations on wage complaints. Jury duty: unpaid time off required.

instrument_name: NJDOL Employer Handbook - Contributions, Wages, Taxable Wages and Exempt Employment (UI/TDI/FLI)
authority: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Employer Accounts
article_or_section: Records; Length of Time to Keep Records; WR-30 Overview and Electronic Filing; Exempt Employment; Wages
figure_or_rule_carried: UI/TDI/FLI wages = all remuneration incl. vacation/holiday pay, back pay, tips reported in writing, service charges, contractual or customary separation pay, employer-paid employee taxes, S-corp officer distributions, employee 401(k)/IRA/deferred-comp deferrals, Section 125 contributions to the extent cash could be elected, dependent care assistance, below-market loans (FUTA rule), personal use of company car (IRC 61), stock options (if cash electable). WR-30 (employee SSN, name, gross wages, base weeks), NJ services only, within 30 days after quarter end, mandatory electronic (online or SFTP); penalties 5/10/25 USD per employee for 1st/2nd/3rd failure in 8 quarters. Domestic-only employers file the four WR-30s with one NJ-927H annually by 30 January. Coverage: domestic employers paying 1,000+ USD cash in a quarter; agricultural employers paying 20,000+ USD cash in a quarter or employing 10+ in 20 weeks; exemptions for students at their school, church services, home-to-home commission salespersons, etc.

authority: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
article_or_section: TDI; FLI; Federal Tax Deductions; Private Plans
figure_or_rule_carried: TDI up to 26 weeks; FLI up to 12 consecutive weeks or 56 intermittent days in 12 months. authority: New Jersey Judiciary (Superior Court Clerk)
article_or_section: order paragraph; How to Calculate Proper Garnishment Amount
